hero.title: Oil Retreats From $110 High as Hormuz Crisis Keeps Global Energy Markets on Edge
hero.description: Brent crude briefly reached almost $110 before falling back towards $104 as markets watched diplomatic efforts to ease shipping disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz.

breaking: 🛢️ Brent crude briefly reaches $109.97 before retreating to around $104.
🇺🇸🇮🇷 Oil remains more than 7% higher this week as the Iran conflict disrupts Middle East energy flows.
🚢 Diplomatic efforts are reportedly under way to improve shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, but no lasting agreement has been reached.
🇺🇸 US diesel prices pass $6 per gallon for the first time as fuel costs surge.
🌍 IEA sharply cuts its 2026 oil supply and demand forecasts as Middle East disruption extends into 2027.
🇳🇬 Dangote Refinery secures at least 16 million barrels of Nigerian crude for October.
🇳🇬 Higher Dangote crude intake could reduce the volume of Nigerian crude available for export.
🇸🇦 Saudi Arabian oil supply falls to its lowest level in more than three decades, according to the IEA.

featured.title: Hormuz Crisis Keeps Oil Above $100 as Fuel Prices Rise
featured.content: Oil prices remain highly volatile after Brent briefly reached $109.97 before retreating. The benchmark is still on course for a weekly gain of more than 7%. Markets are reacting to continuing disruption around the Strait of Hormuz, attacks on energy infrastructure and uncertainty over when normal Gulf oil flows can resume. Reports of diplomatic efforts to improve the movement of ships have provided some relief, but no durable agreement has yet been confirmed.
featured.imageQuery: oil tanker Persian Gulf Strait Hormuz

articles.title: Hormuz Shipping Crisis Keeps Oil Markets Volatile
articles.content: The Strait of Hormuz remains at the centre of the global energy crisis. Oil prices have risen sharply this week as attacks and security concerns reduce the movement of vessels through the strategic waterway. Any prolonged disruption could continue to affect fuel, transport and food costs around the world.

articles.title: Diplomatic Efforts Aim to Ease Gulf Shipping Disruption
articles.content: Middle Eastern countries are exploring arrangements that could improve the movement of commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz. The discussions offer some hope to energy markets, although there is still no confirmed long-term agreement guaranteeing normal shipping.
articles.imageQuery: Gulf countries diplomatic meeting Middle East

articles.title: IEA Warns Energy Disruption Could Extend Into 2027
articles.content: The International Energy Agency has sharply revised its oil outlook as the Iran conflict delays the return of normal Gulf flows. The agency now expects global oil supply to fall by about 5.7 million barrels per day in 2026, while demand is also expected to decline by 2.5 million barrels per day as high prices weaken consumption.

articles.title: Saudi Oil Supply Falls to More Than 30-Year Low
articles.content: The IEA estimates that Saudi Arabia's crude supply fell to around 6 million barrels per day in August, its lowest level in more than three decades. The agency linked the decline to attacks affecting Saudi energy infrastructure and shipping routes.

articles.title: US Diesel Prices Cross $6 Per Gallon
articles.content: US national average diesel prices have moved above $6 per gallon for the first time, according to price tracker GasBuddy. Supply disruptions linked to the Iran conflict and outages affecting Russian refining capacity are putting additional pressure on refined fuel markets.
articles.imageQuery: US diesel fuel station petrol pump

articles.title: Energy Shock Complicates Federal Reserve Outlook
articles.content: Higher fuel prices are creating a difficult policy environment for the Federal Reserve. Energy-driven inflation could make it harder for policymakers to ease monetary policy, while higher household and business costs could simultaneously weaken economic activity.

articles.title: Dangote Secures 16 Million Barrels of October Crude
articles.content: Dangote Refinery has secured at least 16 million barrels of Nigerian crude for October delivery, equivalent to roughly 520,000 barrels per day. The volume represents a substantial share of the refinery's 700,000-barrel-per-day capacity and is significantly above its average intake last year.

articles.title: Nigeria Faces Energy Revenue and Consumer-Cost Dilemma
articles.content: Higher international oil prices could increase Nigeria's export earnings, but the same energy shock can raise transport, electricity, manufacturing and food costs. Dangote's expanding domestic refining activity gives Nigeria another potential advantage, although increased domestic crude purchases can also reduce the volume available for export.

articles.title: Saudi Supply Shock Adds Pressure to African Economies
articles.content: African economies are closely watching the Middle East energy disruption. Oil exporters may benefit from stronger crude prices, while countries that depend heavily on imported fuel face increased pressure on foreign exchange, transportation and household costs.

articles.title: European Markets Remain Sensitive to Energy Prices
articles.content: European markets are being affected by the renewed energy shock as investors assess the possibility that higher oil and fuel prices could keep inflation elevated. The prospect of prolonged monetary tightening is adding to pressure on government bond markets.

articles.title: Undersea Infrastructure Remains a Security Concern
articles.content: European governments continue to focus on the protection of undersea communication and energy infrastructure. Recent reports involving Russian activity near the Arctic have renewed concerns about the vulnerability of cables that carry critical data between countries.

articles.title: China Raises Petrol and Diesel Price Caps
articles.content: China's state planner has announced higher retail price caps for petrol and diesel from September 12. The move reflects the sharp increase in international energy prices and adds to the inflationary pressure facing consumers and businesses.

articles.title: Asian Markets Remain Under Pressure From Oil Shock
articles.content: Asian equities remain sensitive to developments in the Middle East. Investors are assessing how higher energy prices could affect inflation, corporate profits and central-bank policy across major Asian economies.

articles.title: Global Markets Pause After Oil Retreats From Record Weekly High
articles.content: Global bond and equity markets have steadied somewhat after Brent retreated from its $109.97 high. However, investors remain cautious because oil is still more than 7% higher for the week and geopolitical risks remain elevated.

articles.title: Energy Prices Become the Biggest Global Market Risk
articles.content: The latest oil shock is increasingly affecting expectations for inflation, interest rates, transportation and industrial costs. Investors are now watching both diplomatic developments in the Middle East and the ability of producers and refiners to restore disrupted supply.

articles.title: Energy Crisis Highlights Importance of Critical Infrastructure
articles.content: The latest disruption is also drawing attention to the resilience of digital and physical infrastructure. Undersea cables, energy networks, ports and fuel distribution systems are increasingly being treated as strategic assets whose disruption can have consequences far beyond the immediate region.

articles.title: US and Global Consumers Feel the Fuel Shock
articles.content: Record US diesel prices are an important warning sign because diesel powers much of the world's trucking, agriculture, construction and freight industries. Prolonged increases could eventually feed into food prices and the cost of transporting goods.

morningSummary: Good afternoon. The global energy crisis remains the dominant story as Brent crude briefly approached $110 before retreating. US diesel prices have crossed $6 per gallon for the first time, while the IEA warns that the disruption to Middle Eastern oil flows could extend into 2027. In Nigeria, Dangote Refinery has secured at least 16 million barrels of crude for October, strengthening domestic refining activity but also reducing some crude available for export. Ukraine is facing another wave of Russian attacks, while global markets remain highly sensitive to developments around the Strait of Hormuz.
bigQuestion: With energy prices rising again, should oil-producing countries such as Nigeria focus more on increasing crude exports for revenue — or prioritise domestic refining and affordable energy for their own citizens?
